I’ve been feeling like something’s really off for the past couple of months. At first, I thought it was just stress—work’s been hectic, and I’ve been trying to launch this big redesign for a client. But then I started seeing things… like shadows moving in the corner of my apartment, or figures standing across the street who vanish when I look directly. Last week, I swear I saw a man outside my window at night, just staring, but when I turned the light on, no one was there.

I keep thinking the world is… ending, somehow. Not in a metaphorical way—I mean, infrastructure failing, everything collapsing soon. It feels inevitable. I’ve stopped opening my design files because what’s the point if nothing will matter in a few weeks?

There was this stretch a few weeks ago where I hardly slept, but I was hyper-focused—redesigning mockups at 3 a.m., sending dozens of emails, feeling like I could fix everything instantly. My husband said I was talking too fast, like I was on something, but it didn’t feel bad at the time. Now I’m not sure if that energy was real or just part of the breakdown. The visions started before that phase, and they haven’t really gone away, even though the high-energy rush faded after a couple of weeks.
D005-D010_h001.question_a:
I’ve been married for three years now, and things were going well—work was busy but manageable as a UI/UX designer. But about two months ago, everything started to feel… off. I began seeing shadows in my peripheral vision, like figures standing in doorways when no one was there. One night, I clearly saw a man in my bedroom who wasn’t real. It’s not just that—I’m completely certain the world is ending soon. Not like a fear—no, I *know* it. Data centers will collapse, all digital life will vanish, and humanity will be wiped out. There’s no point updating designs anymore. I tried telling my husband, but he just doesn’t get it.

There was this week where I barely slept, full of energy, redesigning our entire apartment layout at 3 a.m., convinced I was preparing for the collapse. But that manic burst lasted only a few days. The visions and the certainty—that we’re all doomed—that’s been constant, day after day, for two full months. Even when the high energy faded, the hallucinations and the truth about the end of the world never left.
D005-D010_h001.question_b:
Lately, everything just feels… apocalyptic. For the past two months, I’ve been seeing shadows of people who aren’t there—figures standing in the corners of rooms, like they’re waiting. I *know* it sounds crazy, but I truly believe the world is ending—something massive and irreversible is coming, and no one else sees it.  

But this all started after this intense burst of energy I can’t explain. I haven’t really needed sleep—like, I’ll stay up three nights straight redesigning app interfaces in my head, and I feel *brilliant*, like my thoughts are faster than everyone else’s. I’ve been spending so much—bought thousands in design software I don’t need, booked a one-way trip to Iceland to “escape the collapse,” and my husband is worried. I told him I’m not sick, that I’m finally *awake*.  

The voices and visions? They only started after this high kicked in. Before this, I was fine—no hallucinations, no doom stuff. But now, they’re here *because* my mind feels so charged, so powerful. When the thoughts slow down, the shadows fade too. It’s like the mania brings them with it—and they vanish when it does.

At first, I thought it was just stress from work—being an insurance agent, especially after my divorce, means I’m on the phone all day, trying to meet quotas. But things got worse. I started believing the world was ending, like a machine in the sky is dismantling reality, part by part. Nothing will survive, not even memories. I know it sounds extreme, but it feels absolutely true.

I catch myself making faces I don’t mean to—like my mouth just twists on its own—especially when I’m alone in my office. My coworkers have noticed. I can’t control it.

There were times I felt wired, like I didn’t need sleep, talking fast, taking on ten projects at once. That lasted a few days a couple of times. But those bursts passed, and the fear and the voices—the ones telling me everything is unraveling—never left. They’ve been constant, even when I’m not feeling “wired.” The paranoia and the grimacing… they’ve been here all four months, straight. It’s like the real me is fading, and I’m just watching.
D005-D010_h014.question_b:
I’ve been really overwhelmed at work lately—closing policies, managing clients, keeping up with deadlines—but my mind’s been racing so fast, I can’t slow it down. For the past four months, I’ve barely needed sleep and still feel wired, like I’m running on pure energy. I’ve been talking fast, jumping between big ideas, convinced I’m about to launch this massive financial platform that’ll change the industry. My coworkers say I seem "off," even theatrical—laughing at serious things or making these weird faces when I’m not even angry.

But here’s what’s scaring me: I’ve started believing the world is ending. Like, literally collapsing. I keep telling my clients to cash out their policies now because there won’t be an insurance system soon. I see it so clearly—it’s not a feeling, it’s *true* to me. I’ve even started acting out in meetings—grimacing, twitching—as if I’m warding off something only I can see.

The thoughts only got this intense during the last four months, and honestly, they seem tied to how high my energy's been. When I feel the mania ramping up, that’s when the delusions and the faces start. Before this, I never had episodes like this—no voices, no paranoia. It’s like the psychosis only shows up when I'm manic.
